people.name: Seth Campbell
people.bio: Glaciologist and geophysicist on the University of Maine Earth and Climate Sciences faculty, and Director of Research for the Juneau Icefield Research Program. A JIRP alumnus (2007), he took over academic and research leadership of the program in 2018 and has worked in many cryosphere field seasons across Alaska, Antarctica, Canada, South America and Greenland.
people.research_interests: Glacier geophysics and remote sensing of glacier dynamics, thermal state and internal structure; permafrost extent and change; geophysical mapping of glacial and sedimentary deposits

people.name: Brad Markle
people.bio: Assistant professor in Geological Sciences and fellow of INSTAAR at the University of Colorado Boulder, and Director of Academics for the Juneau Icefield Research Program, where he has served across more than 13 field seasons since first attending as a student in 2007. He teaches climate, paleoclimate and geochemistry on the Icefield.
people.research_interests: Past climate variability and climate dynamics using ice-core records and models; paleoclimate; geochemistry

people.name: Annie Boucher Krumdieck
people.bio: Director of Operations for the Juneau Icefield Research Program, overseeing non-academic program logistics and coordinating them with the Academic Council. She has returned every season since first joining as a student in 2012, in roles from field staff to assistant operations manager; she holds a geology B.A. from Carleton College.

people.name: Kiya Riverman
people.bio: Environmental Studies faculty member at the University of Portland and Associate Director of Academics for the Juneau Icefield Research Program, which she has joined each summer since 2014, leading projects on seismic and gravity surveys of Taku Glacier, icefield modeling and supraglacial hydrology. PhD in Geosciences, Penn State (2017).
people.research_interests: Glacial hydrology and ice flow; glacier geophysics

people.name: Allen Pope
people.bio: Secretary General of the International Glaciological Society and Associate Director of Academics for the Juneau Icefield Research Program, contributing remote sensing and GIS instruction since first attending as a student in 2007. He holds a PhD in polar studies from Cambridge and previously served as a National Science Foundation program officer.
people.research_interests: Remote sensing and GIS of glaciers; science communication

people.name: Tahi Wiggins
people.bio: Program Manager of the Juneau Icefield Research Program since spring 2026, supporting the Academic Council with field-season planning, curricula and faculty onboarding. She attended JIRP as a student in 2021 and came back in 2024 as research and teaching faculty. She did graduate research on the Icefield for a University of Maine master's in Earth and Climate Science.

people.name: William Field
people.bio: Co-developer of the Juneau Icefield Research Project with Maynard Miller, beginning in 1946 at the American Geographical Society; co-author with Miller of the 1951 publication on exploring the Juneau Ice Cap.

people.name: Joan Miller
people.bio: Co-led the Juneau Icefield Research Program with Maynard Miller from its transition from project to program around 1960 through roughly the following half-century.

people.name: Maynard M. Miller
people.bio: Glaciologist who in 1948 led the reconnaissance of the Juneau Icefield that started the Juneau Icefield Research Program, which he subsequently led with Joan Miller for about half a century; he had earlier studied weather and climate effects on military operations while in the U.S. Navy.

people.name: Mauri Pelto
people.bio: Glacier researcher who teaches environmental science and serves as Associate Provost of Accreditation at Nichols College. He has led the North Cascade Glacier Climate Project as science director since 1983, tracking mass balance on three World Glacier Monitoring Service reference glaciers, and writes the annual alpine glaciers chapter of the BAMS State of the Climate report.
people.research_interests: Glacier response to climate change; glacier mass balance; North Cascades and Juneau Icefield glaciers

people.name: Anne Altman
people.bio: Superintendent of Point Reyes National Seashore since September 2024, after serving there as deputy superintendent from 2022 and acting superintendent from June 2024. A National Park Service manager of more than two decades, she previously held Pacific West Region and Washington headquarters business-management roles; she holds an Earth Systems degree from Stanford and an MBA from UC Davis.

people.name: Ben Becker
people.bio: National Park Service marine ecologist. An NPS contact page last updated in 2016 names him director of the Pacific Coast Science and Learning Center at Point Reyes; his ORCID record lists his position as Science Advisor for the NPS Pacific West Region.

people.name: Timothy R. Newman
people.bio: Program Coordinator of the USGS National Land Imaging Program, which builds and operates the Landsat satellites and maintains one of the world's largest civil archives of land remote sensing data. He directs researchers producing remote-sensing science products. Before USGS he served in space-related U.S. Air Force roles, retiring as a Lieutenant Colonel in 2005.

people.name: Daniel W. Opstal
people.bio: Deputy Program Coordinator of the USGS National Land Imaging Program, handling program guidance, budgets, Administration and Congressional liaison, and international and industry Earth-observation partnerships. Formerly Executive Secretary (now emeritus) of the Civil Applications Committee, coordinating civil use of geospatial technologies with the defense and intelligence community.

people.name: Nathan J. Wood
people.bio: Supervisory research geographer at the USGS Western Geographic Science Center (since 2014), leading its Hazard Vulnerability Team. His research addresses community vulnerability to natural hazards, including exposure, demographic sensitivity and pedestrian evacuation modeling for tsunami, volcanic and coastal threats.
people.research_interests: Societal vulnerability to natural hazards; pedestrian evacuation modeling; geospatial hazard modeling; tsunami, volcanic and coastal hazards
